req.title: Emit OpenAPI schema
req.statement: The system shall serve an OpenAPI 3.x JSON specification at GET /openapi.json.

doc.reasoning: R-PLAYER-017 requires GET /openapi.json to return HTTP 2xx with a valid OpenAPI 3.x JSON payload. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — happy path 200 with correct content-type and openapi version field; (2) negative NEG — wrong HTTP method (POST) returns 4xx; (3) boundary BVA — response body is valid JSON and contains mandatory OpenAPI 3.x top-level keys (openapi, info, paths); (4) DT — info block contains exact title and version matching app metadata; (5) BVA — openapi version string starts with '3.' confirming 3.x compliance. Mutation resilience: exact status code assertions (catches 200->201, 200->204 mutations), exact string equality on version prefix (catches '3.'->'' or '2.' mutations), exact key presence checks (catches key-deletion mutations), exact title/version values from source (catches constant-mutation).

tests.name: test_openapi_json_returns_200
preconditions: GET /openapi.json route is registered by FastAPI automatically
trace: R-PLAYER-017: system shall serve OpenAPI 3.x JSON at GET /openapi.json with HTTP 2xx
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_openapi_json_returns_200():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get('/openapi.json')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert 'application/json' in r.headers.get('content-type', '')

test_openapi_json_returns_200()

tests.name: test_openapi_json_version_is_3x
trace: R-PLAYER-017: specification must be OpenAPI 3.x — version prefix boundary
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_openapi_json_version_is_3x():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get('/openapi.json')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    openapi_version = body['openapi']
    assert isinstance(openapi_version, str)
    assert openapi_version.startswith('3.')
    assert not openapi_version.startswith('2.')
    assert not openapi_version.startswith('1.')

test_openapi_json_version_is_3x()

trace: R-PLAYER-017: payload must reflect app metadata defined in main.py
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_openapi_json_info_matches_app_metadata():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get('/openapi.json')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    info = body['info']
    assert info['title'] == 'python-samples-fastapi-restful'
    assert info['version'] == '1.0.0'

test_openapi_json_info_matches_app_metadata()

tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_openapi_json_paths_contains_players_endpoints():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get('/openapi.json')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.json()
    paths = body['paths']
    assert isinstance(paths, dict)
    assert len(paths) > 0
    assert '/players/' in paths

test_openapi_json_paths_contains_players_endpoints()

tests.name: test_openapi_json_response_is_valid_json_not_empty
actions: Check raw response text is non-empty
trace: R-PLAYER-017: expected payload — response body must be non-empty valid JSON
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
import json

def test_openapi_json_response_is_valid_json_not_empty():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.get('/openapi.json')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert len(r.text) > 0
    parsed = json.loads(r.text)
    assert isinstance(parsed, dict)
    assert len(parsed) > 0

test_openapi_json_response_is_valid_json_not_empty()
